subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed `sessions_spawn` keep returning `accepted` and surface Docker startup failures asynchronously, or preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning?
rationale: The choice affects the public async spawn contract, session registry state, wait semantics, timeout behavior, and overlap with the broader lifecycle-event work.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failures
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make Docker startup failure visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

options.title: Preflight before accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox initialization before the accepted response to fail fast, accepting extra latency and compatibility review for existing callers.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle tracker
options.body: Leave this sandbox-specific issue open while maintainers settle the broader lifecycle contract in #58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failures
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make Docker startup failure visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent adjacent lifecycle work make this the best available owner for the spawn/sandbox contract choice.
